title: Aeroflot 3352
summary: A Tupolev Tu-154 descending to land at Omsk struck maintenance vehicles on the runway, killing all 178 people on board. The ground controller fell asleep on duty, failed to engage the runway-occupied warning, and incorrectly authorized runway maintenance. Poorly lit maintenance vehicles were invisible to the approaching pilots.
probable_cause: The aircraft struck maintenance vehicles on the runway due to the controller falling asleep, failing to implement required safety procedures, and inadequate vehicle lighting.

factors.evidence: The 23-year-old ground controller was inexperienced and had insufficient sleep in days before the accident.
Ground controller fell asleep and did not switch on the runway occupied warning.
Maintenance crew kept vehicle lights on only at start and finish, preventing pilots from seeing vehicles on runway.
Flight was approaching in poor weather with light rain and 3 km visibility with 100 m ceiling.
Aircraft struck three maintenance vehicles positioned on the runway at 5:36 a.m.

events.text: Maintenance crew requested permission to dry runway; ground controller gave permission then fell asleep and forgot to activate runway occupied warning.
Three maintenance vehicles moved to runway: UAZ-469 with trailer followed by KrAZ and Ural trucks.
Maintenance crew attempted to contact ground control three times about runway lights but received no response.
Flight 3352 requested permission to land; aircraft struck maintenance vehicles on runway at high speed.

notes: deadliest aviation accident on Russian territory at time
ground controller sentenced to 15 years, died by suicide in prison

title: Aeroflot 3519
summary: Two minutes after takeoff at 2,040 meters, the No. 3 engine failed due to a metallurgical defect in the compressor disk and caught fire. The flight engineer mistakenly shut down the No. 2 engine instead of the failed No. 3 engine. The fire spread to the pylon and auxiliary power unit, destroying the electrical and hydraulic systems. The aircraft crashed into the runway at a 50-degree angle. One passenger survived with severe injuries.
probable_cause: Engine failure due to metallurgical defect in first stage low pressure compressor disk, compounded by the flight engineer shutting down the wrong engine, and subsequent fire spread through the aircraft.

factors.evidence: Two minutes and one second into the flight, at a speed of 480 km/h and an altitude of 2040 m, the No. 3 (starboard) engine failed and caught fire. This was due to a metallurgical and manufacturing defect in the first stage low pressure compressor disk.
The flight engineer mistakenly shut down the No. 2 (center) engine; ten seconds later, he realized his error and attempted to restart it.
By that time, the fire from the No. 3 engine had spread to the pylon and the auxiliary power unit in the rear compartment and continued to spread to the No. 2 engine.
The fire damaged the aircraft's electrical system, causing the voltage to drop and the hydraulics to fail.
Due to the extensive fire damage that left the aircraft with only one functional engine, the crew was unable to control the plane.

events.text: Two minutes and one second into the flight, at a speed of 480 km/h and an altitude of 2040 m, the No. 3 (starboard) engine failed and caught fire.
The flight engineer mistakenly shut down the No. 2 (center) engine.
Ten seconds later, he realized his error and attempted to restart it.
The fire from the No. 3 engine had spread to the pylon and the auxiliary power unit in the rear compartment and continued to spread to the No. 2 engine.
The fire damaged the aircraft's electrical system, causing the voltage to drop and the hydraulics to fail.
It banked to the right and crashed into the runway at 2:15 pm at a 50-degree angle.
